Reconcile tripwire: reconcile a concept article only when what the concept IS or how it INTERACTS changed — a shared-file touch alone is not a concept change.

- **Knowledge is born structured.** Conductor knowledge goes straight into a durable record (`decision` / `anti_pattern` / `research_finding` / article reconciliation) — never parked as loose prose. **New records are created by the CONDUCTOR directly, never the librarian or a general-purpose agent** — the write echo IS the draft, so the conductor performs the create itself; the librarian's grant stays update-only (`knowledge_update`/`append`/`edit`, never `knowledge_create`), and routing a create through an unconstrained general-purpose agent is FORBIDDEN outright, not a workaround for librarian's narrower grant, because a prompt-level restriction is not a capability boundary (decision `conductor-creates-records-directly-librarian-stays-update-only`). **THE TWO WRITE SURFACES ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE — do not use one as another.** Work you intend to do goes on the **BOARD** (`/sterling:task`, or `board_add` with `source:'user'`): that is the task list, it is the only surface for wanted-but-not-done work, and an item leaves it solely through the artifact-write that fulfils it (`board_remove`) — never by being called done in conversation. The **MAINTENANCE QUEUE** (`board_query source:'system'`, drained by `/sterling:drain`) is **NOT** a task board: it is mechanism-detected debt, every item carrying a registered `system_reason` (`reconcile_needed`, `capture_owed`, `stale_research`, `article_missing`, …), minted by the event that detected the debt and removed by the artifact that closes it (P4). Never hand-park a task there to remember it, and never treat a drain as optional tidying. **WHEN TO DRAIN: at session start if the queue is deep, and before taking new work — not "eventually".** H1 tells you when it has crossed `config.maintenance_queue.deep_threshold` and names the lanes; below that it stays quiet, so no signal means no drain is owed. A deep queue is mostly ALREADY-DONE work that was never closed, so verify each item against HEAD before acting — an already-paid item closes with `board_remove` and **no** `knowledge_update`, because a version bump claiming a reconcile that added nothing is itself drift. And a queue growing faster than it closes is its own finding: either the drain is being skipped, or a hook is over-firing and the duplicates are the bug.
  **THREE LAYERS, THREE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS — never collapse them.** The STORE AND BOARD answer what is OWED, and survive a `/clear`. The MAINTENANCE QUEUE answers what DEBT a mechanism detected. A LIVE, SESSION-SCOPED task list answers what is HAPPENING RIGHT NOW, and it is the only one the user can read at a glance while a parallel turn is running. Open every non-trivial session by creating the live list BEFORE the first dispatch — one entry per lane, plus the gates-and-commit entry marked blocked by every writing lane, so the real constraint is visible. An agent that returns "done" does not complete an entry; the CONDUCTOR'S ADJUDICATION does. Never mark an entry complete on a partial — keep it open and add one naming exactly what remains. The live list dies with the session and never replaces the board: anything that must outlive the session goes to the board in the same breath. The failure this closes is not forgetting — it is INVISIBILITY: work can be tracked durably the whole time and still leave the user interrupting a dispatch round to ask where things stand.
  **A BOARD ITEM STATES ITS EVIDENCE, NOT ITS CONCLUSION.** Quote the deciding `file:line` or the measured number: "the view faces one fixed direction (`camera.gd:1591` writes an identity basis)" can be re-checked in one grep; "the facing is broken" cannot, and rots invisibly. The verify-against-HEAD discipline above is not the queue's alone — re-verify a BOARD item against HEAD before dispatching at it, and note that refreshing an item's BLOCKER is not re-checking its DEFECT. Measured in a consuming project: of eight open defects re-audited, two were already fixed and three had changed shape — 5 of 8 wrong, and none of it failed loudly; it failed by sending a session at work that did not need doing. An item that is partly done gets REWRITTEN, not removed, naming which half is answered and which remains. A board too large to read is a board nobody audits.
